svg.text: Averaged over every season this model ties with
the trend baseline. Restricted to the seasons that
actually broke, it removes 40% of the error — and
flags about half of them in advance, against a
baseline that by construction never flags one.
2025/26 — the season CONAB has not closed
Forecast deviation from each state's own yield trend. The weather in the critical window already happened and is measured; the official yield is still a survey.
PR and MS withheld — their critical windows run into August and the weather series ends 3 Aug 2026, so the window is only 82–85% covered. A truncated window reads to the model as an extreme drought.
The model earns its keep only in the tail
Error removed versus the trend baseline, by how far the season really fell.
Ordinary seasons are 55% of the sample — which is why the average looks like a tie.
Correlation between rainfall anomaly in the critical
window and the yield residual, soybean. Rio Grande
do Sul is four times as sensitive as Mato Grosso —
a national average erases this entirely.
Pearson r, soybean yield residual × rainfall anomaly (z), 1992–2025.
Circled seasons are the ones the model called 10% or more below trend, using only weather and seasons that preceded them.
Dry-day anomaly in the critical window, in standard deviations — the input the model actually reads
